column1: # Publication allowlist — paths where a machine-specific string is EXPECTED.
# This file is data, not comments: check-publication-hygiene.py reads it and
# fails if the prefixes enforced in code and the prefixes recorded here diverge
# in either direction. An exception that exists only in the code is invisible to
# review; one that exists only here does nothing.
# Format: one path prefix per line. Blank lines and `#` comments ignored.
# Why any exception exists at all — the gate's default answer is "no", and an
# exception has to be earned by saying what the string is FOR.
# docs/decisions/
#   An ADR records what was decided and where the work happened. A line like
#   "worktree: /home/<user>/worktrees/epic2" or a verbatim user bug report
#   containing the repository's old clone name is the decision log being honest.
#   Replacing it with a placeholder would make the record vaguer and no more
#   private: the directory name identifies nobody, and the alternative is
#   deleting a true statement about history.
# openspec/changes/
#   A change proposal carries a `Source:` field naming the requirements document
#   it came from. Same argument: that is traceability of a decision. A change
#   whose origin cannot be traced is the defect the field exists to prevent.
# NOT allowlisted, on purpose:
# infra/kiwi/scenarios/ — these carried the same `Source:` header, and they were
#   cleaned instead. The difference is that a Kiwi scenario is a living
#   specification someone reads to write a test, not a record of a past
#   decision, so the path carried no lasting value.
# Test sources (*Test.kt, commonTest, jvmTest) are handled in code rather than
# here: a test that asserts a redactor removes a credential-looking string must
# contain that string.
docs/decisions/
openspec/changes/
